themes.name: Synthetic automation platform upgrade cycle

materiality.reason: Synthetic filings and macro inputs imply enough demand to matter for platform revenue and margins.

novelty.reason: The budget signal is new, but platform leadership was already partially recognized in prior synthetic commentary.

breadth.reason: Synthetic breadth broadened beyond a single symbol, but gains remain concentrated in the platform layer.

durability.reason: Procurement timing supports follow-through, but conversion still depends on real deployment cycles.

timeliness.reason: Core evidence predates the research cutoff; the future notice is explicitly segregated for later monitoring only.

transmission_chain: Synthetic public budgets expand automation pilots.
Integrators prioritize reusable platform vendors over bespoke components.
Platform suppliers capture better attach rates and margin mix.
Improved cash generation and net cash capacity increase optionality.
data_gaps: Production snapshots still need real backlog, quote, and cohort breadth feeds.
Future regulatory confirmation must remain excluded before its availability time.

candidates.name: Demo Automation Platform A
candidates.thesis: Synthetic official facts plus market confirmation support a high-quality continue candidate with enough raw inputs for valuation and cash-structure checks.

bull_case.text: Synthetic filings show revenue scale, operating leverage, positive free cash flow, and net cash, while market data confirm current sponsorship.

bear_case.text: Even in the fixture, adoption could stall if procurement converts slower than expected and attention runs ahead of deployable demand.

risk_verdict.text: Synthetic risk is acceptable for a continue outcome because the candidate has official financial coverage, market confirmation, and explicit invalidation checks.

invalidation_conditions: Synthetic follow-up filings fail to sustain free cash flow or margin progression.
Synthetic market confirmation disappears while breadth narrows back to one name.
manual_review_items: Re-check snapshot cutoff handling before using any future evidence in later runs.

candidates.name: Demo Integrator B
candidates.thesis: Synthetic industry evidence suggests DEMOB could observe the theme, but it lacks the official fact base needed for a stronger stance.

bull_case.text: If platform demand broadens, integrators may see follow-on service pull-through.

bear_case.text: Without issuer-level official evidence, the synthetic benefit path remains indirect and should stay observational.

risk_verdict.text: Synthetic setup looks suitable for observe rather than continue because the financial and market evidence are incomplete.

invalidation_conditions: No synthetic official disclosure emerges tying DEMOB to the budget cycle.
data_gaps: Missing synthetic issuer filing and point-in-time financial facts for DEMOB.
manual_review_items: Require issuer-level official evidence before upgrading beyond observe.
